---
title: Ontologies (OBO)
description: GO, CL, UBERON, MONDO, EFO, DOID, HsapDv and MmusDv from their OBO Graphs JSON releases, as ontology.term and ontology.relationship.
---

Eight ontologies, each from its own versioned
[OBO Graphs JSON](https://github.com/geneontology/obographs) release: the
Gene Ontology (GO), Cell Ontology (CL), UBERON anatomy, MONDO disease, the
Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO), the Disease Ontology (DOID), and the human
and mouse developmental-stage ontologies (HsapDv, MmusDv). The release lands
each file whole, one row per node and one per edge, into `raw.obo__<name>`,
and derives `ontology.term` (every node, obsolete terms kept with
`obsolete = true`) and `ontology.relationship` (every edge). This is GO.db's
content, plus the ontologies the resource and clinical tables point at. The
version is each file's own version IRI.

## Licence and citation

Per ontology, from each release: GO, CL and MONDO CC BY 4.0; UBERON, HsapDv
and MmusDv CC BY 3.0; DOID CC0 1.0; EFO Apache 2.0. Cite each ontology as its
site asks, with the release version.

## Join keys

- `term_id` is a CURIE (`GO:0008150`, `CL:0000084`) where the IRI follows the OBO PURL convention, verbatim otherwise; `ontology` says which file the row came from.
- `ontology.relationship` is (`ontology`, `subject_id`, `predicate`, `object_id`); `predicate` is `is_a` or a relation CURIE, with the common BFO/RO relations as `part_of`, `has_part` and the like.
- `annotation.ncbi__gene_go.go_id`, `clinical.gwas_catalog__association.mapped_trait_ids`, `resource.resource_relationship.target_id` and the eQTL Catalogue tissue ids all join `term_id`.

## Good to know

- A file is whole, not just its own namespace: CL carries BFO, RO, IAO and PR classes referenced in logical definitions, so `ontology.term` has them too.
- A recursive CTE over `is_a` gives descendants; the README's T-cell example shows it.
